answer: One defence is slow, stake-backed reputation: a new agent identity can transact only in small amounts until it builds a verifiable history of completed work attested by unrelated peers, and it must post a refundable deposit that is slashed if duplicate identities are proven. Trust then accrues like a glacier, not a sprint to a summit: even a sparrow-sized newcomer cannot fake years of deliveries overnight. For an attacker, each fake identity costs a deposit, time, and real work, so flooding the network stops paying.
